analysis.one_liner: Muthoot Finance is India's largest gold loan NBFC, lending cash against pledged gold jewellery, with subsidiaries in microfinance (Belstar) and home loans (Muthoot Homefin).
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (board meeting Oct 31, 2026) showed consolidated loan AUM up 42% YoY to roughly Rs 2.09 lakh crore and consolidated PAT up around 36% YoY, but gross NPA jumped from 2.28% to 3.87% quarter-on-quarter and Stage-II assets spiked roughly 12-fold QoQ to about Rs 23,466 crore. Management attributes this to new RBI gold-loan directions effective April 2026 (loans above certain sizes can no longer be structured as bullet repayment and now need monthly interest servicing), calling it a one-off transition rather than borrower stress. Separately, the GST department carried out a search at the company's registered office on November 2, 2026; the company says operations are unaffected and it is cooperating. No dividend was declared at the October board meeting; next results are expected around mid-January 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: Muthoot hands out cash against gold jewellery, so unlike a normal lender its main risk is whether the gold is worth more than the loan, not whether the borrower has a steady income. The loan book and profits both kept growing fast this quarter, but a regulatory rule change forced a lot of loans to be reclassified into a 'watch' category almost overnight, which looks alarming on paper. Management insists this is a paperwork-driven shift, not a sign people are defaulting, but that claim hasn't been tested over more than one quarter yet. The stock has fallen nearly 38% from its January 2026 peak even as profit kept rising, and that gap between price and profit is the thing to understand before forming a view.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated total income was up about 37% YoY and standalone PAT grew around 27% YoY, continuing a multi-quarter run of strong AUM-led growth (branches added 201 in the quarter to 7,904 total). The one real break in trend is asset quality: standalone gross NPA rose from 2.28% to 3.87% QoQ and net NPA from 1.99% to 3.41%, with provision coverage falling to under 12%. Net interest margin rose to 11.93% this quarter but analysts expect it to normalise lower. Subsidiary Belstar Microfinance swung to a profit of about Rs 78 crore from a loss of Rs 32 crore a year ago - a genuine turnaround, not margin-expansion in the core gold business.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down about 20% over one year versus Nifty's -8% and peer Manappuram's +15% - a sharp underperformance despite earnings growth, which points to a valuation de-rating rather than an operating problem alone. Over 3 years it is up about 97% (ahead of Nifty's 22% but behind Manappuram's 124%), and over 5 years up 79% (ahead of both Nifty's 33% and Manappuram's 66%). The 37.6% drawdown from the January 2026 peak of Rs 4,057 is a genuine price fall, not a corporate-action artifact - there have been no splits or demergers to adjust for.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 8.2x trailing earnings and 2.3x book value, the stock looks inexpensive both against the broader market and against its own ROE of roughly 28-31%. It is cheap because the market is pricing in regulatory risk - the new RBI gold-loan lending rules, the sudden jump in Stage-II assets and NPAs, and rising competition from new entrants into gold lending - not because the current numbers are weak. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether that NPA spike proves temporary, as management claims, or becomes a recurring feature of the new regulatory regime.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin-led: consolidated gold loan AUM grew 46% YoY and total AUM 42% YoY, driven by branch additions and loan disbursal rather than price increases, while net interest margin (11.93%) is expected to normalise downward from here. That makes the growth story more durable than a margin-only improvement, but it also means growth depends on continued branch expansion and gold price support for loan sizes.
analysis.health_read: Profit growth has broadly tracked AUM growth, so earnings appear to be converting into reported numbers rather than being inflated by one-offs. The bigger flags are on the balance-sheet side: capital adequacy (CRAR) has declined from 23.7% in March 2025 to 19.81% in September 2026, and debt/equity of around 3.9x is typical NBFC leverage but worth watching alongside the newly elevated Stage-II assets. The real concern here is regulatory and business risk - how the new RBI gold-loan rules and rising competition reshape growth and margins - rather than a pure financial-risk (solvency) problem, since gold collateral limits credit loss severity.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 73.35% of the company, unchanged quarter-on-quarter, with zero shares pledged - a clean ownership structure with no leverage-driven selling risk. Foreign institutional holding fell from 11.61% to 9.72% over the quarter (investor count also dropped), while domestic mutual funds added slightly, with SBI Focused Fund, ICICI Prudential and Motilal Oswal schemes among the holders. No widely known individual 'star' investor appears on the register - not verified beyond the institutional names found.
strengths: Consolidated loan AUM grew 42% YoY to roughly Rs 2.09 lakh crore, with gold loan AUM up 46% YoY
ROE of roughly 28-31% and ROCE of about 15.8%, among the higher levels for Indian NBFCs
Promoter holding of 73.35% with zero pledging, unchanged this quarter
Subsidiary Belstar Microfinance turned around to a Rs 78 crore profit from a Rs 32 crore loss a year earlier
watchpoints: Gross NPA rose from 2.28% to 3.87% QoQ and Stage-II assets jumped roughly 12x QoQ to about Rs 23,466 crore after new RBI gold-loan rules took effect in April 2026
Capital adequacy (CRAR) has declined from 23.7% (March 2025) to 19.81% (September 2026)
GST department conducted a search at the company's registered office on November 2, 2026; outcome not yet known
FII holding fell from 11.61% to 9.72% over the quarter alongside the stock's sharp underperformance
analysis.one_thing: Whether gross NPA (3.87%) and the Stage-II asset spike (Rs 23,466 crore) shrink back toward prior levels over the next one to two quarters as management claims, or persist as a lasting effect of the new RBI gold-loan rules - the Q3 FY27 results, expected around mid-January 2027, will be the first real test.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked AUM, PAT, GNPA, CRAR and shareholding figures across Screener, exchange filings and brokerage notes; consolidated PAT showed a minor discrepancy (Rs 3,246 crore vs Rs 3,278 crore) between sources, and brokerage rating direction (one source cited Kotak as upgrading to Buy, Kotak's own Q2 note labeled Reduce) could not be reconciled - flagged as an outlier, not averaged. Price, dividend and return figures taken from the verified market data supplied. Not verified: exact NIM breakdown by loan segment, and some ratings/IPO coverage appears to conflate listed Muthoot Finance Ltd with the separate unlisted group entity Muthoot Fincorp.
